Effectors and modifiers

Put a field on top of a grid, rules, dashes, rings, type or any SVG. Effectors move, scale, turn, lift and colour each element inside the field. Modifiers then bend, cut, mirror and repeat the outlines themselves. Fields follow the pointer, or move on their own over a seamless loop.

How it works

Recipes

Each recipe is a starting stack. Change anything, or press Shuffle for a random one.

How it works

Elements become clones: every cell, rule segment, dash, arc, letter (or word, or line) and SVG shape is one clone with a position, size, rotation, colour and depth. Effectors change those per clone, in order, each weighted by its field: radial, linear, ring, box, noise or everywhere, soft or hard, inverted or not. A field can follow the pointer, sit still (drag its handle with Show fields on), or orbit, sweep, wander, pulse or rotate. Every motion completes whole cycles in the loop, so the loop repeats seamlessly.

Modifiers come after the effectors and work on outlines. Bending modifiers move every outline point, so long rules and big letters curve smoothly. Cutting modifiers clip outlines along lines and copy them: mirror, kaleidoscope, echo, slice and shatter. Inline rebuilds each outline as concentric bands before it is placed. Stack them in any order; each can target all elements or one.

The modifier set came from a survey of all 1,132 posters in the PosterLab library and all 1,399 in the Japanese archive, looking for distortions that recur. The examples below are where each one shows up; the modifiers are new general constructions, and nothing is traced.
